attacks.claim: The public Recent signers panel prints each signer's full name and full postal code, violating the agreed rule that public signer lists show at most first name, last initial and city. This publishes personal data irreversibly and is cached at the CDN, so rollback does not undo it.
attacks.evidence: • {{ s.full_name }} {{ s.city }} {{ s.postal_code }}

attacks.claim: The newsletter/organizer-updates checkbox is pre-ticked. Under GDPR Art. 4(11) and Art. 7, consent for EU signers must be an affirmative act, so default-on consent to organizer marketing is not valid.
attacks.evidence: <input type="checkbox" id="news" name="newsletter_opt_in" value="1" checked>

attacks.claim: The client handles only 422 and success. A 409 duplicate, 5xx, or network failure produces no visible message, and the aria-live .form-error element is never written, so the signer sees nothing happen.
attacks.evidence: if (res.status === 422) { ... return; } if (res.ok) window.location = res.headers.get('Location'); — no branch for 409 or errors;

attacks.claim: The sign form collects no city, but the Recent signers panel renders {{ s.city }}. No city capture or derivation from postal code is defined, so the city will render empty or undefined.
attacks.evidence: Sign form fields: full_name, email, postal_code only; panel renders {{ s.city }}; ABSENT: any city capture or derivation step

attacks.claim: The success path reads Location from a fetch that follows redirects by default; the final response typically does not expose Location, so window.location may be set to null.
attacks.evidence: const res = await fetch(form.action, { method: 'POST', body: new FormData(form) }); ... if (res.ok) window.location = res.headers.get('Location');

attacks.claim: The duplicate-signature check returns 409 for an already-signed email, letting anyone probe whether a given address signed a specific petition, which reveals political stance (a sensitive category under GDPR Art. 9).
attacks.evidence: Duplicate signature (same email) rejected with 409 | Pass

attacks.claim: Retention for confirmed signatures is not stated; only unconfirmed rows have a 7-day purge, and no erasure or access path for signers is described, conflicting with GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), 15 and 17.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: retention period, deletion schedule, or erasure/access request process for confirmed rows in signatures; Rollback: "flip petitions_signing off" with no data deletion step.

attacks.claim: EU signers' data is routed by a user-entered postal code, and unresolved codes default to us-east-1, so an EU resident with a non-standard code would be stored in the US with no EU fallback. Postal code is also an unreliable proxy for residence.
attacks.evidence: "Postgres, eu-central-1 for EU-resolved postal codes, us-east-1 otherwise"

attacks.claim: EU signers' email addresses are sent to Postmark, a US processor, and the artifact cites only a DPA with no Chapter V transfer mechanism (SCCs or DPF) and no evidence of one.
attacks.evidence: "Confirmation emails go through Postmark; DPA countersigned 2026-09-14" — ABSENT: transfer mechanism for EU signer email data

attacks.claim: The sign endpoint sends a Postmark confirmation for every submission with no rate limit, per-IP or per-address cap, or CAPTCHA, so scripted submissions with arbitrary addresses produce unbounded send volume and cost.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no rate limit, send cap, or bot protection on POST /p/{{ petition.slug }}/sign

attacks.claim: The sign form posts without any CSRF token and no server-side CSRF protection is described, so a third-party page could auto-submit signatures on a signer's behalf.
attacks.evidence: <form class="sign-form" action="/p/{{ petition.slug }}/sign" method="post" novalidate> — ABSENT: CSRF token

attacks.claim: Recent signers renders user-submitted full_name and city; if the template does not auto-escape, this is stored XSS served to every visitor. The artifact does not confirm escaping.
attacks.evidence: • {{ s.full_name }} {{ s.city }} {{ s.postal_code }}

attacks.claim: Rollback does not address CDN cache invalidation. Edge-cached pages keep serving the old sign UI and signer data after the flag flips, and it is not stated whether the Recent signers panel sits behind the flag.
attacks.evidence: Signature counts update live (polling every 15s, cached at the CDN for 10s). Rollback: flip petitions_signing off; no cache purge or panel-flag statement

attacks.claim: The rollout gates on error and bounce rates, but no alert wiring, named owner, or automated rollback trigger is specified, so a regression during the 24h watch depends on manual observation.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: alert thresholds wired to paging, named on-call owner, automated rollback condition

attacks.claim: Rollback does not address pending double-opt-in confirmations or confirmation emails already sent, nor the 7-day purge job's behaviour after the flag is off.
attacks.evidence: Rollback: flip petitions_signing off ... with no statement about pending confirmations or the 7-day purge job.

attacks.claim: Invalid fields are signalled only by red border and background colour, with no text message, aria-invalid, or aria-describedby, so errors are conveyed by colour alone and not associated with fields. This risks failing WCAG 1.4.1 and 3.3.1, which are agreed as required.
attacks.evidence: .sign-form input.is-invalid { border: 2px solid #d93025; background: #fdecea; } — ABSENT: text or aria error association

attacks.claim: WCAG 2.1 AA conformance rests only on an automated axe-core scan of the default page. Error states, the confirmation flow, and the Recent signers panel have no keyboard or screen-reader evidence, although AA is agreed for all public flows.
attacks.evidence: | axe-core automated scan on sign page | 0 violations | — no error-state or manual AT test row

attacks.claim: The load test covers only sign writes at 400/s. The 15s live-count polling and Recent signers render on every petition view are unvalidated at viral read volume.
attacks.evidence: | Load: 400 signatures/s sustained for 10 min, p95 210ms | Pass | ... polling every 15s

attacks.claim: No index is described for the duplicate-email check, per-petition counts, or the Recent signers query (petition, confirmed, created_at), so these can degrade to scans on hot petitions as the table grows.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: index on signatures(petition_id, email) or (petition, confirmed, created_at); Duplicate signature (same email) rejected with 409 | Pass

attacks.claim: A 422 with an empty fields array makes fields[0] undefined, so focus() throws and the error handling itself fails.
attacks.evidence: for (const name of fields) ...; form.elements[fields[0]].focus();

attacks.claim: The submit button is not disabled in flight and no unique constraint on (petition, email) is mentioned, so double-clicks can race past the duplicate check and create duplicate rows.
attacks.evidence: <button type="submit" class="btn-sign">Sign petition</button>; ABSENT: unique index or in-flight guard

attacks.claim: The signing flow never tells the signer that the signature counts only after email confirmation. Someone who ignores the email believes they signed and will be purged after 7 days.
attacks.evidence: unconfirmed signatures are not counted and are purged after 7 days — ABSENT: post-submit message about checking email

attacks.claim: No GDPR Art. 13 privacy notice or lawful basis is referenced for collecting EU signer names, emails and postal codes at the form.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: privacy notice / Art. 13 information and lawful basis in sign form or data handling section

attacks.claim: No unsubscribe or consent-withdrawal path is described for organizer updates.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: unsubscribe / consent withdrawal mechanism for organizer updates

attacks.claim: Confirmed-only and display rules live in a template call, so they are not unit-testable, and the QA claim 'renders 20 most recent confirmed' cannot be verified against the shipped rule.
attacks.evidence: {% for s in petition.recent_signers(limit=20, confirmed_only=True) %}

attacks.claim: The QA pass for the Recent signers panel cannot evidence the agreed privacy display rule, since the template exposes full name and postal code and no QA row checks name or location format.
attacks.evidence: QA table: "Recent signers renders 20 most recent confirmed | Pass"; no QA row checks the name or location format

attacks.claim: The rollback path is asserted but untested; the QA table has no flag-off or rollback row.
attacks.evidence: Rollback: flip petitions_signing off ... vs. QA summary with no rollback row
